evidence.locator: FFFA through FFFF are reserved for vector pointers
evidence.claim: The 6502 takes its NMI, reset and IRQ vectors from $FFFA-$FFFF. This program's thirteen NMI references all depend on that vector table, and its per-frame logic runs from the NMI handler.

evidence.document: Ricoh internal specification, standard number KA-A002-B, section 10 (pin functions)
evidence.transcription: Pin 19, INT, output: VBLANK signal for the CPU interrupt. Pin 18, CLK, input: 21.48 MHz clock.
evidence.claim: The 2C02's INT output is the VBLANK signal wired to the CPU's interrupt input. This is the hardware origin of the NMI that runs this program's per-frame logic, stated by the chip's designer rather than inferred.
evidence.note: Cited as a page image because the document is handwritten Japanese and OCR cannot read it — 'VBLANK' returns zero hits in the extracted text while being plainly legible on the page.

evidence.locator: a write to $3456 is the same as a write to $2006
evidence.claim: PPU register ports mirror every 8 bytes across $2000-$3FFF, so the program's $2006/$2007 writes are the canonical addresses rather than the only ones that would work.
OAMDMA at $4014 takes the high byte of a page and copies it into OAM — the mechanism this program uses to update sprites each frame.

evidence.locator: accessible by writing the bottom 3 bits of $4016
evidence.claim: Controller strobe and read run through $4016, which is how this program reads player input.

note: The NES has no boot ROM, so this proof has no restricted input and runs its execute stage in public CI as well as locally — the only machine here whose rendered frame is checked on every push.
evidence_caveat: Tiers and media are both explicit because the NES sources differ in kind. Two items are PRIMARY: MOS's programming manual for the 6502 vector table, and Ricoh's own internal specification for the 2C02 — the latter cited as a hash-pinned page image, because the document is handwritten and no text locator could ever match it. The remaining items are EXTERNAL-FORMAL: the NESdev wiki, community documentation built from hardware analysis. No Nintendo-published programming manual exists to acquire; the 2A03 and 2C02 are semi-custom parts that never had a public datasheet, so the designer's internal specification is the primary document rather than a substitute.
